newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper slumps to seven week lows near close.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper slumps to seven week lows near close.

text.p: COMEX copper futures fell sharply to seven week lows near the close Wednesday, with LME copper sharply lower in London also.

"The move just caught everyone asleep," one trader said. "There's no news behind it, just a break key support levels around 88 cents, basis December, followed by decent volume trade and fund selling."

COMEX December copper was down 2.80 cents a lb at 87.20 cents, after trading down to a session low at 87.00 cents, its lowest level since July 22. In London, three month LME futures fell below $1,900 a tonne for the first time in seven weeks.
The December/March backwardation narrowed sharply to 0.95 cents though, from 1.50 cents at Tuesday's close.
COMEX copper warehouse stocks were down 500 short tons to 20,602 short tons Tuesday.

In the past few days both COMEX copper and LME copper prices have been consolidating near the bottom of the range of the past two months, after swinging in a wide range last week, partly on options related trade as short positions, established during the Sumitomo affair earlier this year, were unwound.

"Prices have been susceptible to another technical selloff though," one analyst said. "But a number of U.S. producers continue to buy copper in the spot market to meet sales commitments which could moderate the extent of any price decline."
--Clive McKeef, New York Commodities Desk, phone +1-212-859-1640; email: clive.mckeef@reuters.com
